01The bottleneck
The KV-cache is the fastest-growing cost in LLM decode.

Every generated token re-reads the whole key/value cache. It scales with context length and comes to dominate on-device memory and bandwidth — so the host spends its energy moving the cache, not computing.

02The block

Do the cache work at the edge of memory

Three hardened engines behind a serial loader — the host streams tokens in and reads compressed records back.

KVE · compress

CQ-3-rot value path

Walsh–Hadamard rotation + per-token amax + INT3 quantization → rotated INT3 codes and one fp16 scale per token. Synthesizable, bit-exact vs. reference.

TIU · score

H2O token importance

Heavy-hitter scoring across cache slots → a per-slot keep-tier bitmap and one eviction-victim slot, so cold tokens leave first.

ACU · gate

Precision controller

A divide-free per-tile gate over the importance distribution → a keep-fp16 decision when a tile is peaky enough to warrant it.

Everything streams over a 4-wire SPI slave — 6 functional pins + 4 status bits.

03Architecture

One serial link in, compressed records out

Host writes V + W, pulses START, polls STATUS, then reads CODES / SCALE / V̂ + the decision byte — all over the same four wires.

07Physical

The hardened block

final_core/gds/lambda_kv_coproc.gds
  • 502.89 × 520.81 µm core, no padring — a pre-integration macro.
  • GF180MCU · 180 nm, 5 V — mcu7t5v0 standard cells.
  • Text-labelled pins — obs0..obs3, VDD/VSS and the SPI signals, matched by name.
  • Timing closed at 300 ns across all signoff corners.
08Integration

Slots into the org padframe by name

  • We submit a core-only block + an info.yaml pin list.
  • The org generates the padframe, sized to our area, and returns a DEF.
  • Placed in a BV slot — 1/8, 16 pins, ground on pin 1. We use 12; unused slots become analog pads.
  • Delivered BV + BH variants — both reconcile against our submission exactly.

09Verification

Proven, and reproducible

  • Self-checking SPI test — write W + V, START, poll STATUS, read back decision / keep-bitmap / codes / scale. All checks pass.
  • CI rebuilds it — simulation + hardening on every push.
  • LVS ties the layout back to the netlist — the GDS is what the RTL says.

Calibrated: verification is at the RTL + physical-signoff level. Gate-level simulation and exhaustive coverage are named future work, not implied here.
